title: Vanishing mean after coordinate restriction
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, subset $S$ of the coordinates with $|S|\ge2$, coordinate $i\in S$, and value $\omega\in\Omega$, the product mean of the orthogonal component of $f$ indexed by $S$, with coordinate $i$ fixed to $\omega$, is zero.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ containing the constant-one function
$S$ is a subset of the coordinates with $|S|\ge2$
